scope: Dated, source-backed hydraulic and crop-calendar evidence for the Greater Angkor footprint. This is a physical-feature packet, not a population target and not an Angkor-specific correction.

feature_records.geography: Tonle Sap and Lower Mekong floodplain; applicable to Angkor only through the mapped flood-recession/deepwater setting
feature_records.observation: Traditional deepwater rice is grown in wet-season flood depths and uses varieties elongating approximately 2–3 m; floating-rice varieties can elongate approximately 5–6 m.
feature_records.model_use: Create a shared, date-compatible flood-depth/crop-calendar mask and uncertainty scenario. Plant height is not converted directly to yield or population.

feature_records.geography: Tonle Sap River/Lake and Mekong-Bassac branches; includes the Angkor-region ecological regime
feature_records.observation: Flood-recession rice uses receding wet-season water trapped by embankments, ponds and dams to irrigate dry-season crops through canals and/or pumps; conventional rain-fed or irrigated rice is not the correct representation for continuously flooded sites.
feature_records.model_use: Add a generic flood-recession production pathway competing for land and water with ordinary rain-fed and irrigated rice. Apply only where sampled flood-seasonality, elevation and conveyance features satisfy the mask.

feature_records.observation: Large barays, canals and bunded paddy fields made managed wet-rice production possible; Angkor depended in part on deepwater/floating and flood-recession rice around Tonle Sap.
feature_records.model_use: Supply a cited technology-compatibility mask and a shared hydraulic-efficiency prior. Do not copy the mapped Angkor field area into all feasible land.

feature_records.geography: Angkor as described by Zhou Daguan
feature_records.observation: A Chinese visitor reported cultivation of three to four rice crops per year. The report does not identify the land share, crop types, or whether the count combines irrigated and flood-recession environments.
feature_records.model_use: Upper crop-calendar scenario for the relevant flood/irrigation mask only; never apply 3–4 cycles to all Angkor land and never treat the travel account as a population label.
caveats: possible mixing of ecological production systems

feature_records.observation: Archaeobotanical macroremains document rice processing/consumption and pulses, including mung bean, pigeon pea and yardlong bean, during continued fourteenth- and fifteenth-century occupation.
feature_records.model_use: Validate the crop-family availability mask and protein-diversity pathway. Do not infer yield or population from sample counts.

feature_records.geography: Angkor Borei, approximately 10 km radius; not Greater Angkor
feature_records.observation: Fox and Ledgerwood estimate that 80,000 farm workers using flood-recession cultivation could support an additional 40,000 people within a 10 km radius.
feature_records.model_use: Held-out physical validation of a generic flood-recession pathway after land, calorie, protein and labor accounting. It is out of period for 1337 Angkor and cannot set global scale.

current_eu5_diagnostic.interpretation: The crop/water label matrix is closed, but the current score has no generic dated flood-recession/deepwater-rice pathway or shared hydraulic-efficiency scenarios. This is a missing physical feature implementation, not a missing label and not permission for a named Angkor multiplier.

sources.citation: Fox, J. and Ledgerwood, J. (1999), 'Dry-season flood-recession rice around the Mekong and Angkor Borei'; summarized in The Evolution of Rice Farming in the Lower Mekong Basin.
Klassen et al. (2021), Diachronic Modeling of the Population within the Medieval Greater Angkor Region Settlement Complex, Science Advances 7(19), eabf8441.
sources.source_role: independent archaeological settlement and population context; not a local-food target
